Every chapter, blind checkpoint, and capstone in the 30-chapter **Advanced Strings & Combinatorics on Words** textbook enforces a single, unambiguous system of mathematical notation, index boundaries, and local algebraic hypotheses. Bookmark this page to cross-check indexing rules, border/period dualities, automaton state invariants, or structural failure modes across [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd).

---

## 1. Indexing Conventions, Alphabets, and Fundamental Word Operations

Stringology sits at the crossroads of combinatorics on words—where 1-based closed intervals $S[l..r]$ align prefix lengths with right endpoints—and polynomial/modular algorithms—where 0-based indices $0, \dots, N-1$ align with FFT/NTT exponents and residue classes. We standardize on **1-based closed indexing $S[1..N]$** throughout the textbook, with explicit 0-based exceptions only where polynomial degrees or modular residues require them.

::: {.callout-important title="Canonical Textbook Indexing Contract (`1-Based Closed` $S[1..N]$ vs. `0-Based` Polynomial/Residue Offsets)"}
1. **Default 1-Based Closed Indexing ($S[1..N]$)**:
   - A string $S$ of length $N = |S|$ is indexed as $S = S[1]S[2]\cdots S[N]$.
   - For $1 \le l \le r \le N$, the contiguous substring $S[l..r] = S[l]S[l+1]\cdots S[r]$ has length **$|S[l..r]| = r - l + 1$**.
   - Whenever $l > r$, $S[l..r] = \varepsilon$ denotes the unique **empty word** of length $|\varepsilon| = 0$.
   - Why 1-based closed intervals eliminate off-by-one bugs:
     - The $i$-th prefix $S[1..i]$ has length **exactly $i$** (so $\pi[i]$ is the longest proper border length of the length-$i$ prefix).
     - A proper border of length $b \in [0, i-1]$ of $S[1..i]$ satisfies $S[1..b] = S[i-b+1..i]$, corresponding to period $p = i - b$.
     - A substring of length $L$ ending at position $e \in \operatorname{endpos}_S(u)$ starts at **$s = e - L + 1$**, so it lies completely inside $S[l..r]$ if and only if **$e \in [l + L - 1, r]$** ([`Ch 10`](chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd)).
2. **When 0-Based Indexing Is Used**:
   - **Polynomial / FFT String Matching ([`Ch 18`](chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd)–[`Ch 19`](chapters/ch19-kmismatch-wavefront-period-dichotomy.qmd))**: Pattern $P[0..M-1]$ and text $T[0..N-1]$ are indexed from $0$ so character $P[j]$ maps directly to monomial $x^j$, and index-reflected pattern $P^R[k] = P[M-1-k]$ places alignment shift $i$ at Cauchy product degree $M - 1 + i$:
     $$\sum_{j=0}^{M-1} f(P[j])\,g(T[i+j]) = [x^{M-1+i}] \left(\sum_{k=0}^{M-1} f(P[M-1-k]) x^k\right)\left(\sum_{t=0}^{N-1} g(T[t]) x^t\right).$$

   - **Modular Residue Classes ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 03`](chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd))**: Residue vertices in $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ are indexed $0, 1, \dots, m-1$.
   - **2-Adic Popcount Sequences & Word-RAM Bit-Blocks ([`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd), [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd))**: The Prouhet–Thue–Morse infinite word $T[0..\infty)$ with $T[n] = \operatorname{popcount}(n) \bmod 2$, 64-bit machine word-block arrays `VP[0..W-1]`, and $0$-indexed Unit-Monge permutation border ports $P[0..K-1]$.
:::

### 1-Based vs. 0-Based Translation Reference

| Operation / Boundary | Canonical 1-Based Closed $S[1..N]$ | 0-Based Half-Open $S[0..N)$ / Closed $S[0..N-1]$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Length-$k$ Prefix of $S$** | $S[1..k]$ (ends at index $k$) | $S[0..k)$ or $S[0..k-1]$ (ends at index $k-1$) |
| **Length-$k$ Suffix of $S$** | $S[N-k+1..N]$ (starts at $N-k+1$) | $S[N-k..N)$ or $S[N-k..N-1]$ (starts at $N-k$) |
| **Substring Length** | $\lvert S[l..r]\rvert = r - l + 1$ | $\lvert S[l..r)\rvert = r - l$, or $\lvert S[l..r]\rvert = r - l + 1$ |
| **Start of Length-$L$ Factor Ending at $e$** | $s = e - L + 1 \ge l \iff e \ge l + L - 1$ | $s = e - L + 1 \ge l \iff e \ge l + L - 1$ |
| **Z-Array Match Span at Index $i$** | $S[1..Z[i]] = S[i..i+Z[i]-1]$ ($i \in [1..N]$) | $S[0..z[i]-1] = S[i..i+z[i]-1]$ ($i \in [0..N-1]$) |
| **Manacher Unified Center $c \in [1..2N-1]$** | Odd center $S[i] \leftrightarrow c = 2i-1$; Even gap $S[i..i+1] \leftrightarrow c = 2i$ | Odd center $S[i] \leftrightarrow c = 2i$; Even gap $\leftrightarrow c = 2i+1$ |

### Fundamental Word & Alphabet Symbols

| Symbol / Notation | Formal Definition & Canonical Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\Sigma,\; \sigma = \lvert\Sigma\rvert$ | Finite totally ordered alphabet $(\Sigma, <)$ of size $\sigma = \lvert\Sigma\rvert$. Unless stated otherwise, $\Sigma = \{1, \dots, \sigma\}$ or $\{0, \dots, \sigma-1\}$. |
| $\Sigma^*,\; \Sigma^+,\; \Sigma^n$ | Free monoid of all finite words over $\Sigma$ (with identity $\varepsilon$), semigroup of nonempty words $\Sigma^+ = \Sigma^* \setminus \{\varepsilon\}$, and set of words of exact length $n$. |
| $\lvert S\rvert,\; \lvert S\rvert_c$ | Length of word $S$, and number of occurrences of character $c \in \Sigma$ in $S$. |
| $\operatorname{Parikh}(S)$ | Parikh (frequency) vector $(\lvert S\rvert_{c_1}, \dots, \lvert S\rvert_{c_\sigma}) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^\sigma$ ([`Ch 20`](chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd)). |
| $S[l..r]$ | Contiguous substring (factor) $S[l]S[l+1]\cdots S[r]$ of length $r - l + 1$ ($1 \le l \le r \le \lvert S\rvert$), or $\varepsilon$ if $l > r$. |
| $S^R$ | Reversal (mirror image) of $S$: $S^R[i] = S[\lvert S\rvert - i + 1]$ for $1 \le i \le \lvert S\rvert$. A word $S$ is a **palindrome** iff $S = S^R$. |
| $U \cdot V$ or $UV,\; S^k,\; S^\omega$ | Concatenation of words $U$ and $V$; $k$-fold repetition $S^k = SS\cdots S$ ($S^0 = \varepsilon$); and infinite right-periodic repetition $S^\omega = SSS\cdots$. |
| $U \sqsubseteq_{\text{pref}} S,\; U \sqsubset_{\text{pref}} S$ | $U$ is a prefix (respectively, proper prefix, $\lvert U\rvert < \lvert S\rvert$) of $S$. When clear from context, written $U \sqsubseteq S$ and $U \sqsubset S$. |
| $U \sqsubseteq_{\text{suf}} S,\; U \sqsubset_{\text{suf}} S$ | $U$ is a suffix (respectively, proper suffix, $\lvert U\rvert < \lvert S\rvert$) of $S$. |
| $U \sim_{\text{conj}} V$ | **Conjugacy (Cyclic Shift Equivalence)**: $\exists X, Y \in \Sigma^*$ such that $U = XY$ and $V = YX$ ([`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)). |
| $\text{prim}(S),\; \exp(S)$ | **Primitive Root & Exponent**: The unique shortest word $w$ such that $S = w^k$ ($k \ge 1$); $w$ is **primitive** ($\exp(w) = 1$). |

## 2. Periodicity, Border Algebra, and Series-Link (`slink`) Notation (`Part I`)

Every proper border of $S[1..N]$ is complementary to a weak period of $S[1..N]$. All periodicity and border DP chapters ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd)) build upon three foundational identities:

1. **Period–Border Duality ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd))**: For $b \in [0, N-1]$ and $p = N - b \in [1, N]$,
   $$b \in \operatorname{Border}(S) \iff S[1..b] = S[N-b+1..N] \iff \forall i \in [1, N-p],\; S[i] = S[i+p] \iff p = N - b \in \operatorname{Per}(S).$$

2. **Fine–Wilf Threshold & Sub-Threshold Orbit Identity ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd))**: If $p, q \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ and $N \ge p + q - \gcd(p, q)$, then $\gcd(p, q) \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$. Below threshold ($\max(p, q) \le N < p + q - \gcd(p, q)$), the period constraints partition $\{1, \dots, N\}$ into **exactly $C(N; p, q) = p + q - N$ independent character orbits**.
3. **Half-Open `slink` Partition & Shift-Overlap Identity ([`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd))**: By the Weak Periodicity Lemma, all borders/palindromic suffixes of state $u$ of length $\ge \lceil\operatorname{len}[u]/2\rceil$ share period step $d = \operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{len}[u] - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]$. Grouping contiguous ancestors with equal $\operatorname{diff}$ into **half-open** chains $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ yields $\le \lceil\log_2 N\rceil$ chains whose left endpoints $\mathcal{I}(u, r) = \{r - \ell : \ell \in (\operatorname{slink}[u], u]\}$ satisfy the **Shift-Overlap Identity**:
   $$\operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{diff}[\operatorname{fail}[u]] = d \implies \mathcal{I}(u, r) = \mathcal{I}(\operatorname{fail}[u], r - d) \sqcup \bigl\{r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d\bigr\}.$$

| Symbol / Array | Formal Definition & Structural Invariant | Primary Chapters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\operatorname{Per}(S)$ | Set of all **weak (general) periods** of $S$: $\{p \in [1, \lvert S\rvert] : S[i] = S[i+p]\;\forall 1 \le i \le \lvert S\rvert - p\}$. Note that $\lvert S\rvert \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ always corresponds to the empty border $b = 0$. | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 03`](chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{per}(S)$ (or $p_{\min}(S)$) | **Shortest (minimum) period** of $S$: $\operatorname{per}(S) = \min \operatorname{Per}(S) = \lvert S\rvert - \operatorname{bd}(S) = \lvert S\rvert - \pi[\lvert S\rvert]$. We say $S$ is **periodic** if $\operatorname{per}(S) \le \lvert S\rvert / 2$, and a **full period (cyclic root)** if $\operatorname{per}(S) \mid \lvert S\rvert$. | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{Border}(S)$ | Set of all **proper borders** (lengths or strings) of $S$: $\{b \in [0, \lvert S\rvert - 1] : S[1..b] = S[\lvert S\rvert - b + 1..\lvert S\rvert]\}$. | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{bd}(S)$ | **Longest proper border length** of $S$: $\operatorname{bd}(S) = \max \operatorname{Border}(S) = \lvert S\rvert - \operatorname{per}(S)$. | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd) |
| $\pi[i]$ | **KMP Prefix Function**: $\pi[i] = \operatorname{bd}(S[1..i]) = \max\{b \in [0, i-1] : S[1..b] = S[i-b+1..i]\}$ for $1 \le i \le N$, with $\pi[1] = 0$. | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 27`](chapters/ch27-inverse-reconstruction-inequality-dags.qmd) |
| $Z[i]$ | **Z-Function**: $Z[i] = \operatorname{LCP}(S[1..N], S[i..N])$ for $1 \le i \le N$ ($Z[1] = N$). | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd), [`Ch 27`](chapters/ch27-inverse-reconstruction-inequality-dags.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{fail}[u]$ | Longest proper border (in KMP, $\operatorname{fail}[i] = \pi[i]$) or longest proper palindromic suffix (in PAM) of state $u$. | [`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{diff}[u]$ | **Local Period Step**: $\operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{len}[u] - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]$ (in KMP, $\operatorname{diff}[u] = u - \pi[u] = \operatorname{per}(S[1..u])$). | [`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{slink}[u]$ | **Series Link (`等差数列跳链`)**: Highest ancestor of $u$ in the same period-step chain: $\operatorname{slink}[u] = \operatorname{slink}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]$ if $\operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{diff}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]$, else $\operatorname{fail}[u]$. Represents the half-open AP $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ whose shortest member has length $\operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] + \operatorname{diff}[u]$. | [`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{anc}[u]$ | **KMP Shortcut Mismatch Link**: $\operatorname{anc}[u] = \pi[u]$ if $S[\pi[u]+1] \neq S[u+1]$, else $\operatorname{anc}[\pi[u]]$. An exact coarsening of $\operatorname{slink}[u]$ because $\operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{diff}[\pi[u]] \implies S[\pi[\pi[u]]+1] = S[\pi[u]+1]$. | [`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd) |
| $g[u]$ | **Series-Link Rolling DP Accumulator**: Aggregates $dp[r - \ell]$ over all lengths $\ell$ in the half-open chain $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ via $g[u] = dp[r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - \operatorname{diff}[u]] \oplus ([\operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{diff}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]] \cdot g[\operatorname{fail}[u]])$. | [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd) |

## 3. Lyndon Theory, Significant Suffixes, and Runs Notation (`Part II`)

In [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd), lexicographical comparisons are decomposed into **prefix containment** ($\sqsubset_{\text{pref}}$) and **strong mismatch order** ($\prec$):

- **Standard vs. Strong Lexicographical Order ([`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)–[`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd))**:
  $$U <_{\text{lex}} V \iff (U \sqsubset_{\text{pref}} V) \;\lor\; (U \prec_{\text{lex}} V), \qquad U \prec_{\text{lex}} V \iff \exists k \le \min(|U|, |V|) : U[1..k-1] = V[1..k-1] \land U[k] < V[k].$$
  When clear from context, $\prec_{\text{lex}}$ is written $\prec$. Crucially, strong order is **invariant under arbitrary right-extensions** ($U \prec V \implies UT \prec VT\;\forall T \in \Sigma^*$), whereas proper-prefix containment $U \sqsubset_{\text{pref}} V$ can flip when a right-extension $T$ is appended.

- **Reverse-Alphabet Order $\overline{\prec}$ (or $<_>, \prec_>$) ([`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd))**:
  $$U \;\overline{\prec}\; V \quad(\text{also written } U \prec_> V) \iff V \prec_{\text{lex}} U, \qquad U <_> V \iff (U \sqsubset_{\text{pref}} V) \;\lor\; (U \;\overline{\prec}\; V).$$
  Note that under $<_>$, a proper prefix $U \sqsubset_{\text{pref}} V$ is **still smaller** than $V$! Thus $\operatorname{rk}_>$ must be computed on the character-inverted string $\overline{S}[t] = \sigma + 1 - S[t]$ with terminal sentinel $\$ = 0 = -\infty$ fixed, never by negating $-\operatorname{rk}_<$ (`BP-07`).

- **Tandem-Annihilation of Candidate Suffixes ([`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd))**: If $u, v$ are suffixes of $S[l..r]$ with $|u| < |v| < 2|u|$ and $u \sqsubset_{\text{pref}} v$, then $u = w u'$ and $v = w^2 u'$ ($|w| = |v|-|u|$), so for **every** right-extension $T \in \Sigma^*$:
  $$\min(u'T, vT) <_{\text{lex}} uT <_{\text{lex}} \max(u'T, vT),$$
  eliminating $u$ and bounding $|\operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[l..r])| \le \lfloor\log_2(r-l+1)\rfloor + 1$.

| Symbol / Object | Formal Definition & Structural Meaning | Primary Chapters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $U <_{\text{lex}} V,\; U \prec_{\text{lex}} V$ | Standard lexicographical order ($U \sqsubset V$ or $U \prec_{\text{lex}} V$) vs. **strong (mismatch) order** ($U <_{\text{lex}} V$ and $U \not\sqsubset V$). | [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |
| $\overline{\prec}$ (or $<_>, \prec_>$) | Lexicographical order over the inverted alphabet $(\Sigma, >)$, where proper prefixes remain smaller ($U \sqsubset V \implies U <_> V$) and mismatches reverse ($U \;\overline{\prec}\; V \iff V \prec_{\text{lex}} U$). | [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |
| $U \preceq_\omega V$ | **Infinite Periodic Order**: $U^\omega \le_{\text{lex}} V^\omega \iff UV \le_{\text{lex}} VU$ (governs greedy string concatenation and Bijective BWT cycle sorting). | [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 28`](chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd) |
| $\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_<,\; \mathcal{L}_>$ | Set of **Lyndon words** under $<$ (respectively $>$): nonempty primitive words strictly smaller than all their proper suffixes ($w \in \mathcal{L} \iff \forall v \sqsubset_{\text{suf}} w,\, w \prec_{\text{lex}} v$). | [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{CFL}(S)$ | **Chen–Fox–Lyndon Factorization**: Unique tuple $(w_1, w_2, \dots, w_k)$ with $S = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_k$, $w_i \in \mathcal{L}$, and $w_1 \ge_{\text{lex}} w_2 \ge_{\text{lex}} \cdots \ge_{\text{lex}} w_k$. | [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd), [`Ch 28`](chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[l..r])$ | **Significant Suffixes (`显著后缀`)**: Set of suffixes $u$ of $S[l..r]$ for which $\exists T \in \Sigma^*$ making $uT$ the unique shortest lexicographically minimal suffix of $S[l..r]T$; satisfies $\lvert\operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[l..r])\rvert \le \lfloor\log_2(r-l+1)\rfloor + 1$. | [`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd) |
| $\lambda_<[i],\; \lambda_>[i]$ | **Lyndon Array**: Length of the longest $<$-Lyndon (respectively $>$-Lyndon) prefix of $S[i..N]$, satisfying $i + \lambda_<[i] = \min\{j \in [i+1, N+1] : \operatorname{rk}_<[j] < \operatorname{rk}_<[i]\}$. | [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |
| $R = (l, r, p)$ (or $[l, r, p]$) | A **Run (Maximal Periodic Repetition)**: substring $S[l..r]$ of minimum period $p = \operatorname{per}(S[l..r]) \le (r - l + 1)/2$ that cannot be extended left ($l=1$ or $S[l-1] \neq S[l+p-1]$) or right ($r=N$ or $S[r+1] \neq S[r-p+1]$) with period $p$. | [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd), [`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd) |
| $e(R) = \exp(R)$ | **Exponent of Run $R = (l, r, p)$**: rational number $e(R) = \frac{r - l + 1}{p} \ge 2$. | [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |
| $\mathcal{R}(S)$ | Set of all runs of $S[1..N]$. By **Bannai et al.'s Runs Theorem**, $\lvert\mathcal{R}(S)\rvert \le N - 1 < N$ and $\sum_{R \in \mathcal{R}(S)} e(R) < 3N$. | [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |
| $\text{L-root}(R)$ | **Lyndon Root of Run $R = (l, r, p)$**: under mismatch order $<_R \in \{<, >\}$ defined by $S[r+1] <_R S[r+1-p]$, the unique conjugate $S[i..i+p-1] \in \mathcal{L}_{<_R}$ starting at an interior index $i \in [l+1, l+p]$ with $\lambda_{<_R}[i] = p$. | [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd) |

## 4. Suffix Structures, Palindromic Automata, and Internal Queries (`Parts III–IV`)

Across [`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd), suffix trees, suffix automata, enhanced suffix arrays, and internal dictionaries are unified by three structural dualities:

1. **Three-Way Suffix Tree Isomorphism ([`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 13`](chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd))**:
   $$\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S) \;\cong\; \mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}\bigl(\operatorname{SAM}(S^R)\bigr) \;\cong\; \operatorname{Min-CartesianTree}\bigl(\operatorname{height}[2..N]\bigr).$$

2. **Substring Containment Clipping on $\operatorname{SAM}(S)$ ([`Ch 10`](chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd))**: A string $P$ of length $L$ belonging to $\operatorname{SAM}(S)$ state $u$ occurs inside $S[l..r]$ if and only if
   $$L \le r - l + 1 \quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{endpos}_S(u) \cap [l + L - 1,\, r] \neq \emptyset.$$

3. **Bounded-Ratio Internal Pattern Matching (`IPM`) Single-AP Theorem ([`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd))**: For any substrings $U, V$ of $S$ with $|U| \le |V| < 2|U|$, all occurrences of $U$ inside $V$ overlap on a common core of length $> 0$ and form a **single arithmetic progression** with common difference $d = \operatorname{per}(U)$.

| Symbol / Function | Formal Definition & Structural Meaning | Primary Chapters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\operatorname{SA}[1..N],\; \operatorname{rk}[1..N]$ | **Suffix Array & Inverse Suffix Array**: $\operatorname{SA}[k]$ is the starting index of the $k$-th lexicographically smallest nonempty suffix of $S$; $\operatorname{rk}[\operatorname{SA}[k]] = k$ (with terminal sentinel $\operatorname{rk}[N+1] = 0$). | [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd), [`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)–[`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd), [`Ch 27`](chapters/ch27-inverse-reconstruction-inequality-dags.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{height}[2..N]$ (or $h[k]$) | **Adjacent LCP Array**: $\operatorname{height}[k] = \operatorname{LCP}(\operatorname{SA}[k-1], \operatorname{SA}[k])$ for $2 \le k \le N$. For $1 \le i \neq j \le N$ with $r_1 = \min(\operatorname{rk}[i], \operatorname{rk}[j])$ and $r_2 = \max(\operatorname{rk}[i], \operatorname{rk}[j])$, $\operatorname{LCP}(i, j) = \min_{r_1 < k \le r_2} \operatorname{height}[k]$. | [`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)–[`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{LCE}(i, j) = \operatorname{LCP}(i, j)$ | **Longest Common Extension (Forward)**: $\max\{\ell \ge 0 : S[i..i+\ell-1] = S[j..j+\ell-1]\}$. Dual backward extension: $\operatorname{LCS}_S(i, j) = \operatorname{LCE}_{S^R}(N-i+1, N-j+1)$. | [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd), [`Ch 13`](chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd), [`Ch 19`](chapters/ch19-kmismatch-wavefront-period-dichotomy.qmd), [`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{endpos}_S(u)$ | **End-Position Equivalence Class** in $\operatorname{SAM}(S)$: $\{r \in [1, N] : S[r-\lvert w\rvert+1..r] = w\}$ for any $w$ represented by state $u$. Forms a laminar tree hierarchy with $\le 2N - 1$ states and $\le 3N - 4$ DAG transitions. | [`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)–[`Ch 11`](chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd), [`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{len}(u),\; \operatorname{link}(u),\; \operatorname{minlen}(u)$ | **SAM State Span**: $\operatorname{len}(u)$ is the longest string in state $u$; $\operatorname{link}(u)$ is the parent of $u$ in $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\operatorname{SAM}(S))$; state $u$ covers all suffixes of its longest string of lengths in $[\operatorname{minlen}(u), \operatorname{len}(u)]$ where $\operatorname{minlen}(u) = \operatorname{len}(\operatorname{link}(u)) + 1$. | [`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)–[`Ch 11`](chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd), [`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{IPM}(U, V) = \operatorname{Occ}(U, V)$ | **Internal Pattern Matching**: Starting positions of substring $U = S[l_1..r_1]$ inside $V = S[l_2..r_2]$; returns a single arithmetic progression $(a_0, d = \operatorname{per}(U), c)$ in $O(1)$ time when $\lvert V\rvert < 2\lvert U\rvert$. | [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd) |
| $r_{\text{odd}} = 1,\; r_{\text{even}} = 0$ | **Palindromic Tree (`PAM` / `Eertree`) Roots**: Odd root of length $\operatorname{len}[1] = -1$ (for single-letter centers) and even root of length $\operatorname{len}[0] = 0$ (for $\varepsilon$ and even centers), with $\operatorname{fail}[0] = 1$. | [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd) |
| $\texttt{quick\_link}[u][c]$ | **Unamortized Direct Fail Link in PAM**: Deepest proper palindromic suffix $v$ of $u$ preceded by character $c$ ($S[r - \operatorname{len}[v]] = c$), computed in $O(1)$ upon node creation: $\texttt{quick\_link}[u][c] = \operatorname{fail}[u]$ if $S[r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]] = c$ else $\texttt{quick\_link}[\operatorname{fail}[u]][c]$. | [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd) |
| $\texttt{trans}[u],\; \texttt{max\_pref},\; \texttt{max\_suff}$ | **Half-Palindrome Pointer** ($\le \lfloor\operatorname{len}[u]/2\rfloor$) and **4-Way Deque PAM Surface Arrays** maintaining the longest palindromic prefix/suffix at active deque endpoints $[L..R]$ in worst-case $O(1)$ time via lazy surface push-down. | [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{Pal}(S),\; L_{\text{rich}}[r]$ | Set of distinct palindromic substrings of $S$ (including $\varepsilon$). By **Droubay–Pirillo**, $\lvert\operatorname{Pal}(S)\rvert \le \lvert S\rvert + 1$; $S[l..r]$ is a **Rich Word** ($\lvert\operatorname{Pal}(S[l..r])\rvert = r - l + 2$) iff $l \ge L_{\text{rich}}[r]$. | [`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd) |

## 5. Algebraic, Automaton, Subsequence, Seaweed & Group Notation (`Parts V–VII`)

In [`Ch 18`](chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd)–[`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd), combinatorial string transitions are compiled into linear operators, formal power series, Unit-Monge permutation braids, and non-abelian matrix groups. Alongside every formula that divides or inverts a matrix, we record its **local algebraic hypothesis**:

1. **Goulden–Jackson Overlap Polynomials & Moment-Shifted Generating Functions ([`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)–[`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd))**:
   For patterns $P_i, P_j \in \Sigma^+$, the **Guibas–Odlyzko correlation polynomial** and **bivariate $(t-1)$ cluster system** are
   $$C_{i,j}(x) = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Overlap}(P_i, P_j)} x^{|P_j| - k}, \qquad F_S(z) = \frac{z^{|S|}}{(1-z)\,C_{S,S}(z/\sigma)\,\sigma^{|S|} + z^{|S|}},$$
   where $k \in \operatorname{Overlap}(P_i, P_j) \iff 1 \le k \le \min(|P_i|, |P_j|)$ and $P_i[|P_i|-k+1..|P_i|] = P_j[1..k]$. Because $[x^0]\mathbf{C}(x) = I_m$, the matrix $\mathbf{C}(x)$ is invertible in $\mathcal{R}[[x]]^{m \times m}$ over **any commutative ring $\mathcal{R}$**. Substituting $t = 1 + u$ collapses the denominator of $[u^j]F(x, 1+u)$ to $(1 - \sigma x)^{j+1}$ (requiring $\sigma \in \mathcal{R}$ and $(j!)^{-1} \in \mathcal{R}^\times$ when converting binomial moments to power moments).

2. **Invertible Subsequence Automaton (`DASG`) Matrices ([`Ch 22`](chapters/ch22-dasg-arch-simon-invertible-matrices.qmd))**:
   In the distinct-subsequence DP over $S[1..N]$ on state vector $\mathbf{dp} = (dp_{c_1}, \dots, dp_{c_\sigma}, 1)^\top$, reading character $c$ multiplies by the elementary $(\sigma+1)\times(\sigma+1)$ matrix $M_c$:
   $$M_c = I_{\sigma+1} + \mathbf{e}_c \mathbf{1}^\top, \qquad \det(M_c) = 1 \in \mathcal{R}^\times, \qquad M_c^{-1} = I_{\sigma+1} - \mathbf{e}_c(\mathbf{1} - 2\mathbf{e}_c)^\top \quad (\text{or } I_{\sigma+1} - \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{e}_c \mathbf{1}^\top \text{ on total-sum basis}).$$
   *Local Algebraic Hypothesis*: Over the coordinate basis $(dp_{c_1}, \dots, dp_{c_\sigma}, 1)^\top$ where $M_c$ replaces row $c$ by $\sum_{j=1}^{\sigma+1} dp_j$, the column operation is unitriangular with $\det(M_c) = 1$, so $M_c^{-1}$ is **100% division-free in every commutative ring $\mathcal{R}$** (including characteristic $2$); the alternative $1 - \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{e}_c\mathbf{1}^\top$ form on the total-sum state requires $2 \in \mathcal{R}^\times$.

3. **Tiskin's Seaweed Matrices & Unit-Monge Braid Product $P \boxdot Q$ ([`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd))**:
   For strings $A[1..M]$ and $B[1..N]$, the second cross-difference of semi-local LCS scores is a $(M+N)\times(M+N)$ **Seaweed Permutation Matrix** $P_{A,B}$. Its **distribution matrix** $D^\Sigma_P$ and **Unit-Monge distance product ($\boxdot$)** are defined by
   $$D^\Sigma_P(r, c) = \sum_{x \ge r,\; y < c} P(x, y), \qquad (D^\Sigma_P \odot_{\min,+} D^\Sigma_Q)(i, k) = \min_{j} \bigl(D^\Sigma_P(i, j) + D^\Sigma_Q(j, k)\bigr) = D^\Sigma_{P \boxdot Q}(i, k),$$
   composable in $O((M+N)\log(M+N))$ time via Tiskin's monotone-staircase divide-and-conquer.

| Symbol / Operator | Formal Definition & Algebraic Contract | Primary Chapters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\operatorname{clip}(v, \ell)$ | **Window-Clipped Offset Operator**: $\operatorname{clip}(v, \ell) = v$ if $v \le \ell$, else $0$. Restores prefix-suffix monotonicity to predecessor offsets $\operatorname{prev}_S[i] = i - \operatorname{last}[S[i]]$ (`p-KMP`) and Cartesian parent distances $\operatorname{PD}_S[i]$ (`Cartesian-KMP`). | [`Ch 20`](chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd) |
| $\gamma(S),\; S_\tau = \mathsf{Sync}_\tau(S)$ | **Kempa–Prezza String Attractor** ($\gamma(S) = \min\lvert\Gamma\rvert$ hitting every distinct substring, equivalent to hitting $\operatorname{minlen}(u)$ of every SAM state $u$) and **Kempa–Kociumaka $\tau$-Synchronizing Set** $S_\tau$ of size $O(N/\tau)$. | [`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{DASG}(S),\; \iota(S),\; \sim_k$ | **Directed Acyclic Subsequence Graph** ($\operatorname{nxt}[i][c] = \min\{j > i : S[j] = c\}$), **Universality Index $\iota(S)$** from Hébrard's Arch Factorization ($\operatorname{sas}(S) = \iota(S) + 1$), and **Simon's Congruence** $U \sim_k V$ (identical subsequences of length $\le k$). | [`Ch 22`](chapters/ch22-dasg-arch-simon-invertible-matrices.qmd) |
| $M_c,\; M_c^{-1},\; \mathbf{u}_r^\top \cdot \mathbf{v}_{l-1}$ | **DASG Transition Matrix & $O(\sigma)$ Matrix-Free Range Query**: Precomputing $\mathbf{u}_r^\top = \mathbf{e}_{\sigma+1}^\top P_r$ and $\mathbf{v}_{l-1} = P_{l-1}^{-1}\mathbf{1}$ in $O(1)$ per character answers range $[l, r]$ distinct subsequences via $\mathbf{u}_r^\top \cdot \mathbf{v}_{l-1}$ in $O(\sigma)$ time without segment trees ($\det M_c = 1$). | [`Ch 22`](chapters/ch22-dasg-arch-simon-invertible-matrices.qmd) |
| $V' = X \mathbin{\&} \sim(X - Y)$ | **Allison–Dix 4-Instruction Bit-Parallel LCS Identity**: Given row-difference bitmask $V$ ($\Delta_j = dp[i][j] - dp[i][j-1] \in \{0, 1\}$), $X = V \mid M_{A[i]}$ and $Y = (V \ll 1) \mid 1$ propagate hardware subtraction borrows across 64 columns in $O(1)$ operations. | [`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd), [`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd) |
| $P \boxdot Q,\; D^\Sigma,\; W[1..N]$ | **Unit-Monge Seaweed Braid Product ($\boxdot$) & Distribution Matrix $D^\Sigma$**: Bottom-port seaweed array $W[1..N]$ gives $\operatorname{LCS}(A[1..i], B[l..r]) = \#\{k \in [l, r] : -i \le W[k] < l\}$ in $O(\log N)$ via 2D dominance counting. | [`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd) |
| $C_{i,j}(x),\; F_S(z),\; \Omega_{A,B}$ | **Goulden–Jackson Overlap Polynomial $C_{i,j}(x)$, Stopping PGF $F_S(z)$ & Martingale Wealth**: $\Omega_{A,B} = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Overlap}(A, B)} \mathbb{P}(B[1..k])^{-1}$ ($\mathbb{E}[T_S] = \Omega_{S,S} = F_S'(1)$), and division-free pattern-race weight $\Phi_{i,j} = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Overlap}(P_i, P_j)} \mathbb{P}(P_j[k+1..\lvert P_j\rvert])$. | [`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)–[`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{LF}(i),\; \operatorname{BBWT}(S)$ | **Burrows–Wheeler Last-to-First Mapping** $\operatorname{LF}(i) = C[L[i]] + \operatorname{rank}_{L[i]}(L, i)$ and sentinel-free **Bijective BWT** built from cyclic shifts of $\operatorname{CFL}(S)$ factors under $\preceq_\omega$. | [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 28`](chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd) |
| $\operatorname{red}(S[l..r]),\; M_c \in GL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ | **Free-Group / Stack Reduction** of $S[l..r]$: isomorphic to simple tree path $u_{l-1} \leadsto \operatorname{LCA}_{\mathcal{T}}(u_{l-1}, u_r) \leadsto u_r$ on the deterministic **Stack-Trie $\mathcal{T}$**, and hashed by trace-zero $\det = -1$ involution matrices $M_c = \begin{pmatrix} a_c & b_c \\ (1-a_c^2)/b_c & -a_c \end{pmatrix}$ ($M_c^2 = I_2, b_c \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times, p > 2$). | [`Ch 29`](chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd) |
| $\varphi^k(S),\; w_k$ | $k$-fold **Iterated Substitutive Morphism** $\varphi : \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ ($\varphi^0(S) = S, \varphi^k(S) = \varphi(\varphi^{k-1}(S))$), and **Rytter's Singular Words** $w_k = \operatorname{invert}(F_k[f_k]) F_k[1..f_k-1]$ giving $F_\infty = w_0 w_1 w_2 \cdots$. | [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd) |

## 6. Master Atlas of the 24 Structural Boundary Pitfalls (`BP-01`–`BP-24`)

Throughout [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd), every algorithmic contract explicitly inoculates against a canonical set of stringology bugs and Sturmian/Fibonacci edge cases:

| ID | Boundary Pitfall Name | Broken Shortcut / Counterexample Witness | Exact Structural Rescue & Primary Chapter |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BP-01`** | **Sub-Threshold Fine–Wilf Fallacy** | Assuming $p, q \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ implies $\gcd(p,q) \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ at $\lvert S\rvert = p+q-\gcd(p,q)-1$ (fails on `abaababaaba` for $(5,8), N=11$) | Only $N \ge p+q-\gcd(p,q)$ forces $\gcd(p,q)$; below threshold, exact orbit count is $p + q - N$ ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)) |
| **`BP-02`** | **Closed-Interval `slink` Double-Counting** | Treating $[\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ as closed double-counts the chain boundary node $\operatorname{slink}[u]$ across adjacent AP blocks | Enforce the **half-open invariant $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$** with shortest member $\operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] + \operatorname{diff}[u]$ ([`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd)) |
| **`BP-03`** | **0-1 vs. Unbounded Residue-Cycle Deque Push Order** | Pushing old $D_{\text{old}}[v_t] - t \cdot d_k$ before updating $D[v_t]$ in `[WC2016] 论战捆竹竿` restricts each AP pass to a 0-1 step | Update $D[v_t]$ from `dq.front()` **first**, then push updated $D[v_t] - t \cdot d_k$ for unbounded period reuse ([`Ch 03`](chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd)) |
| **`BP-04`** | **Oldest-Element `g[u]` Initialization Bug** | Initializing `g[u] = dp[r - len[u]]` in PAM/KMP `slink` DP ($r - \operatorname{len}[u]$ is already inside `g[fail[u]]`!) | Initialize `g[u] = dp[r - len[slink[u]] - diff[u]]` (the single newly entering element at the short end) ([`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd)) |
| **`BP-05`** | **Odd-Index `g[u]` Update Omission in Interleaved PAM** | Skipping `g[u]` updates at odd indices $r$ in `CF 932G` / `CF 906E` when an even $r$ with odd $\operatorname{diff}[u]$ reads `g[fail[u]]` from odd $r - d$ | Always update `g[u]` at **every** index $r$ (both odd and even); gate only the outer `dp[r]` accumulation on $2 \mid r$ ([`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd)) |
| **`BP-06`** | **Left-Truncation Non-Inclusion of Significant Suffixes** | Assuming $\operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[l..r]) \subseteq \operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[1..r])$ (on `aaba`, index $2$ `aba` is killed on $[1,4]$ by index $1$, but revives on $[2,4]$!) | Maintain candidate sets per segment-tree node with 1-survivor `pushup` or query dyadic SA-RMQ bands on $[l, r]$ ([`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd)) |
| **`BP-07`** | **The $S = \texttt{bab}$ Negated-Rank Trap for $\lambda_>[i]$** | Using $-\operatorname{rk}_<[i]$ to simulate reverse order $<_>$ reverses proper-prefix containment ($\texttt{bab} <_> \texttt{b}$ falsely holds!) | Build $\operatorname{rk}_>$ on character-inverted string $\overline{S}[t] = \sigma + 1 - S[t]$ with sentinel $0 = -\infty$ fixed ([`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd), [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)) |
| **`BP-08`** | **Leftmost vs. Rightmost Square Density Trap** | Assuming $\le 2$ squares start at any index $i$ ($\Theta(\log N)$ primitive squares start at $i=1$ in Fibonacci words!) | Crochemore–Rytter's $\le 2$ bound holds only for the **last (rightmost) occurrences** of distinct squares ([`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)) |
| **`BP-09`** | **GSAM Zero-Length Clone & $\Theta(V^2)$ Trie-DFS Bug** | Calling single-string `extend(c)` after `last = 1` on `{"ab", "b"}` creates a dead clone with $\operatorname{len}(u)=\operatorname{len}(\operatorname{link}(u))$; Trie-DFS takes $\Theta(V^2)$ on `a^k b` | Use the **3-Case GSAM Rule** (allocate only `clone` in Case 3) and traverse the Trie in **BFS order** for $O(V\sigma)$ time ([`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)) |
| **`BP-10`** | **Unclipped `endpos` Left-Boundary Overflow** | Querying $\operatorname{endpos}(u) \cap [l, r] \neq \emptyset$ for a pattern of length $L$ matches substrings starting at $e - L + 1 < l$ | Always clip the left query boundary to **$[l + L - 1, r]$**, and shrink $L$ to $e_{\max} - l + 1$ before jumping to $\operatorname{link}(u)$ ([`Ch 10`](chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd)) |
| **`BP-11`** | **Unflushed LCT Lazy Tag on Dynamic SAM `clone` Split** | Splitting $q \to \text{clone}$ in online LCT-SAM without splaying $q$ leaves un-pushed path-add tags above $q$ | Call `access(q); splay(q);` before reading `cnt[q]` and linking `clone` in Dynamic LCT-SAM ([`Ch 11`](chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd)) |
| **`BP-12`** | **Intra-State SAM Length-Tie Cycle Bug** | Connecting $B_j$ directly to SAM node $u$ in `[十二省联考 2019]` allows a longer $B_j$ to transition to a shorter $A_i$ in the same state | Sort substrings inside each SAM node $u$ by length (placing $B$ before $A$ on ties $\lvert B_j\rvert = \lvert A_i\rvert$) ([`Ch 11`](chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd)) |
| **`BP-13`** | **Character-Only LMS Substring Comparison in `SA-IS`** | Comparing LMS-substrings by characters only without their $(S[\cdot], \operatorname{type}(\cdot))$ pairs merges suffixes with opposite continuations | Two LMS-substrings are equal iff their lengths, characters, **and $L/S$ types** match at every offset ([`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)) |
| **`BP-14`** | **Suffix Balanced Tree `push_back` Order Collapse** | Attempting `push_back(c)` on a Suffix Balanced Tree flips relative order of existing suffixes (`a` vs. `ab` + `z`) | Suffix Balanced Trees support **only front updates (`push_front` / `pop_front`)**; reverse the string if online append is needed ([`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)) |
| **`BP-15`** | **One-Sided Dyadic IPM Border Check Failure** | Checking only prefix $P_m = S[l..l+2^m-1]$ in `[BJWC2018]` accepts false borders (`W = ababacababab`, $b=6$) | Intersect **both** the prefix AP $\operatorname{Occ}(P_m, \text{tail})$ and the suffix AP $\operatorname{Occ}(Q_m, \text{head})$ ([`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd)) |
| **`BP-16`** | **Deque PAM Whole-Deque Palindrome Update Omission** | Updating only `last_suff` when a pushed character creates a palindrome spanning the entire deque ($\operatorname{len}[w] = R - L + 1$) | Whenever $\operatorname{len}[w] = R - L + 1$, set **both** `last_pref = last_suff = w` and use lazy surface push-down on `pop` ([`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)) |
| **`BP-17`** | **Single-Node vs. Subtree `last_end` in Range Palindromes** | Reading only `last_end[u]` instead of the fail-subtree maximum when sweeping Range Distinct Palindromes | A longer palindrome $v$ in $u$'s fail-subtree refreshes $u$'s occurrence at $r' - \frac{\operatorname{len}[v]-\operatorname{len}[u]}{2}$; query Euler-tour subtree max ([`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd)) |
| **`BP-18`** | **Cubic ASCII Modulo-$998244353$ Overflow in Wildcard NTT** | Using raw ASCII codes $c \in [97, 122]$ in $\sum P_j T_{i+j}(P_j - T_{i+j})^2$ overflows $998244353$ and causes false-zero wrap-around | Use **Degree-Reduced Indicator Encoding** $u_c \in \{0, 1\}, v_c \in [1, \sigma]$ so $D_{\text{ind}}(i) \le M(\sigma-1)^2 \ll 998244353$ ([`Ch 18`](chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd)) |
| **`BP-19`** | **Unclipped Predecessor Offset in `p-KMP` / `Cartesian-KMP`** | Comparing raw $\operatorname{prev}_T[i]$ against $\operatorname{prev}_P[q+1]$ fails when $T[i]$ occurred before the current match window $i - q$ | Always compare **window-clipped offsets** $\operatorname{clip}(\operatorname{prev}_T[i], q) == \operatorname{prev}_P[q+1]$ ([`Ch 20`](chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd)) |
| **`BP-20`** | **Non-Terminating RLE Block Mismatch in SLP LCE** | Recursing into the next block of a Locally Consistent Parse Tree when RLE exponents $\ell_1 \neq \ell_2$ match on character $c$ | Terminate immediately at the first RLE block with $\ell_1 \neq \ell_2$ and add $\min(\ell_1, \ell_2)$ ([`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd)) |
| **`BP-21`** | **Singular Matrix Inversion on Gap-2 or Tropical Subsequence DP** | Attempting prefix-matrix inversion $P_{l-1}^{-1}$ on gap $\ge 2$ (`ABC 214 F`, $\det = 0$) or tropical $(\min, +)$ DP (`CF 750E`) | Matrix inversion requires $\det M_c \in \mathcal{R}^\times$ (`Ch 22`); singular or tropical transition matrices require Segment Tree / Bakuri ([`Ch 22`](chapters/ch22-dasg-arch-simon-invertible-matrices.qmd)) |
| **`BP-22`** | **Non-Antichain Embedded Factor Omission in Goulden–Jackson** | Running standard Goulden–Jackson when $P_a \subset P_b$ without filtering to an antichain or absorbing internal weights | Filter $\mathcal{P}$ to an antichain for avoidance, or absorb internal factor weights into $\widetilde{W}_j, \widetilde{C}_{i,j}$ ([`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)) |
| **`BP-23`** | **Missing Root `is_pal[k][r]` Bit in Signed Parallel DSU** | Returning early when `rx == ry` and `rel == 1` in Signed Binary-Lifting DSU misses self-palindrome constraints ($S[1..4] = S[1..4]^R$) | Set `is_pal[k][rx] = 1` when `rx == ry && rel == 1`, and push $B_{k-1}(r) = B_{k-1}(r+2^{k-1})^R$ down ([`Ch 26`](chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd)) |
| **`BP-24`** | **Un-Indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Cancellation on Directed Dyck Strings** | Multiplying un-indexed $M_{\texttt{(}} = A, M_{\texttt{)}} = A^{-1}$ cancels `)(` inside `(( )( ))` even though prefix balances stay $\ge 0$ | Use **Deterministic Stack-Trie Path Isomorphism** or **height-indexed generators $M_{(c, \operatorname{bal}[i])}$** ([`Ch 29`](chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd)) |

## 7. Worked Hand-Checkable Trace on the Fibonacci Word $F_6 = \texttt{abaababa}$ ($N = 8$)

To make the notation above concrete, the table below traces all primary prefix and suffix arrays on the 1-based Fibonacci word $S[1..8] = \texttt{abaababa}$ ($\Sigma = \{\texttt{a}=1, \texttt{b}=2\}$, terminal sentinel $\$ = 0$ at index $9$):

| Index $i$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ | Invariant / Identity Illustrated |
| :--- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :--- |
| $S[i]$ | $\texttt{a}$ | $\texttt{b}$ | $\texttt{a}$ | $\texttt{a}$ | $\texttt{b}$ | $\texttt{a}$ | $\texttt{b}$ | $\texttt{a}$ | $F_6 = \pi_6 \cdot \texttt{ba}$, where central palindrome $\pi_6 = \texttt{abaaba}$ has periods $3, 5$ and length $3+5-\gcd(3,5)-1 = 6$ ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)) |
| $\pi[i]$ (KMP) | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $2$ | $3$ | $\operatorname{Border}(S[1..8]) = \{3, 1, 0\}$; $\operatorname{Per}(S[1..8]) = \{8-b\} = \{5, 7, 8\}$ |
| $\operatorname{diff}[i] = i - \pi[i]$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $3$ | $3$ | $3$ | $5$ | $5$ | At $i=8$: $\operatorname{diff}[8]=5 \neq \operatorname{diff}[3]=2$, so $\operatorname{slink}[8] = 3$ |
| $\operatorname{slink}[i]$ (KMP) | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $2$ | $3$ | Chain $(\operatorname{slink}[8], 8] = (3, 8]$ has single member $8$; $(\operatorname{slink}[3], 3] = (0, 3]$ has $\{1, 3\}$ |
| $Z[i]$ | $8$ | $0$ | $1$ | $5$ | $0$ | $3$ | $0$ | $1$ | $Z[4] = 5$ witnesses $S[1..5] = S[4..8] = \texttt{abaab}$, so $p = 4-1 = 3 \in \operatorname{Per}(S[1..8])$ |
| $\operatorname{SA}[i]$ | $8$ | $3$ | $6$ | $1$ | $4$ | $7$ | $2$ | $5$ | Sorted suffixes: $\texttt{a}$ ($8$), $\texttt{aababa}$ ($3$), $\texttt{aba}$ ($6$), $\texttt{abaababa}$ ($1$), $\texttt{ababa}$ ($4$), $\texttt{ba}$ ($7$), $\texttt{baababa}$ ($2$), $\texttt{baba}$ ($5$) |
| $\operatorname{rk}_<[i]$ | $4$ | $7$ | $2$ | $5$ | $8$ | $3$ | $6$ | $1$ | Inverse of $\operatorname{SA}$ ($\operatorname{rk}_<[9] = 0$); descents $\operatorname{rk}[i] > \operatorname{rk}[i+1]$ occur at $L$-types $i \in \{2, 5, 7, 8\}$ ([`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)) |
| $\operatorname{height}[i]$ | — | $1$ | $1$ | $3$ | $3$ | $0$ | $2$ | $2$ | $\operatorname{LCE}(1, 4) = \min_{4 < k \le 5} \operatorname{height}[k] = \operatorname{height}[5] = 3$ ($\texttt{aba}$) |
| $\lambda_<[i]$ ($<$-Lyndon) | $2$ | $1$ | $5$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $1$ | $i + \lambda_<[i] = \operatorname{nsv}_{\operatorname{rk}_<}[i]$: at $i=3$ ($\operatorname{rk}_<[3]=2$), next smaller rank is $j=8$ ($\operatorname{rk}_<[8]=1$), so $\lambda_<[3] = 8 - 3 = 5$ ($\texttt{aabab} \in \mathcal{L}_<$) |
| $\lambda_>[i]$ ($>$-Lyndon) | $1$ | $3$ | $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | Built on $\overline{S} = \texttt{babbabab}$ ($\operatorname{rk}_>[1..8] = [6,2,8,5,1,7,3,4], \operatorname{rk}_>[9]=0$): at $i=2$, $\lambda_>[2]=3$ ($\texttt{baa} \in \mathcal{L}_>$) |
| $\operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[1..i])$ | $\{1\}$ | $\{1\}$ | $\{3,1\}$ | $\{4,3,1\}$ | $\{3\}$ | $\{6,3\}$ | $\{6,3\}$ | $\{8,6,3\}$ | At $i=8$: candidate starting positions $\{8, 6, 3\}$ have lengths $\{1, 3, 6\}$ (`a`, `aba`, `aababa`), strictly doubling at every step ([`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd)) |

### Complete Enumeration of Runs $\mathcal{R}(F_6)$, Palindromes $\operatorname{Pal}(F_6)$, and PAM `slink` Chains on $S = \texttt{abaababa}$

1. **Maximal Periodic Runs $\mathcal{R}(\texttt{abaababa})$ ([`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd))**:
   - $R_1 = (l=1, r=8, p=3) = \texttt{abaababa}$: exponent $e(R_1) = 8/3 = 2.667$. At the right boundary $r=8=N$, choosing $>-$order gives unique interior $>-$Lyndon root $i = 2$ ($S[2..4] = \texttt{baa} \in \mathcal{L}_>$, $\lambda_>[2] = 3 = p$).
   - $R_2 = (l=3, r=4, p=1) = \texttt{aa}$: exponent $e(R_2) = 2/1 = 2$. Right mismatch $S[5] = \texttt{b} > S[4] = \texttt{a}$ selects $<_{R_2} = \,>$, with unique interior $>-$Lyndon root $i = 4$ ($S[4..4] = \texttt{a}$, $\lambda_>[4] = 1 = p$).
   - $R_3 = (l=4, r=8, p=2) = \texttt{ababa}$: exponent $e(R_3) = 5/2 = 2.5$. Right boundary $S[9] = \$ < S[7] = \texttt{b}$ selects $<_{R_3} = \,<$, with interior $<$-Lyndon roots $i \in \{4, 6\}$ where $\lambda_<[4] = \lambda_<[6] = 2 = p$ ($S[4..5] = S[6..7] = \texttt{ab} \in \mathcal{L}_<$).
   - Note that the period-$3$ repetition $S[2..7] = \texttt{baabab}$ extends left to $l=1$ and right to $r=8$, so it is absorbed into $R_1 = (1, 8, 3)$.
   - Total runs: $|\mathcal{R}(F_6)| = 3 < 8 = N$, with pairwise disjoint interior Lyndon root sets $\{2\} \sqcup \{4\}_> \sqcup \{4, 6\}_< \subseteq \{2..8\}$, and exponent sum $\sum_{R \in \mathcal{R}(F_6)} e(R) = \frac{8}{3} + 2 + \frac{5}{2} = \frac{43}{6} \approx 7.167 < 3N = 24$.

2. **Palindromic Tree (`PAM`) States & `slink` Chains on $S = \texttt{abaababa}$ ([`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd))**:
   - Every prefix $S[1..r]$ ($1 \le r \le 8$) creates a new unioccurrent longest palindromic suffix, so $|\operatorname{Pal}(F_6)| = 8 + 1 = 9 = N + 1$ (**$F_6$ is a Rich Word**, $L_{\text{rich}}[1..8] = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]$):
     - Roots: odd root $1$ ($\operatorname{len} = -1$) and even root $0$ ($\operatorname{len} = 0, \operatorname{fail} = 1$).
     - $r=1$ (`a`): $\operatorname{len}=1, \operatorname{fail}=0, \operatorname{diff}=1, \operatorname{slink}=0$.
     - $r=2$ (`b`): $\operatorname{len}=1, \operatorname{fail}=0, \operatorname{diff}=1, \operatorname{slink}=0$.
     - $r=3$ (`aba`): $\operatorname{len}=3, \operatorname{fail}=\texttt{a}(1), \operatorname{diff}=2, \operatorname{slink}=\texttt{a}$.
     - $r=4$ (`aa`): $\operatorname{len}=2, \operatorname{fail}=\texttt{a}(1), \operatorname{diff}=1, \operatorname{slink}=0$ (merges with $\texttt{a}$ since $\operatorname{diff}[\texttt{aa}] = \operatorname{diff}[\texttt{a}] = 1$).
     - $r=5$ (`baab`): $\operatorname{len}=4, \operatorname{fail}=\texttt{b}(1), \operatorname{diff}=3, \operatorname{slink}=\texttt{b}$.
     - $r=6$ (`abaaba`): $\operatorname{len}=6, \operatorname{fail}=\texttt{aba}(3), \operatorname{diff}=3, \operatorname{slink}=\texttt{aba}$.
     - $r=7$ (`bab`): $\operatorname{len}=3, \operatorname{fail}=\texttt{b}(1), \operatorname{diff}=2, \operatorname{slink}=\texttt{b}$.
     - $r=8$ (`ababa`): $\operatorname{len}=5, \operatorname{fail}=\texttt{aba}(3), \operatorname{diff}=2, \operatorname{slink}=\texttt{a}$ (merges with $\texttt{aba}$ into the half-open AP chain $(\texttt{a}, \texttt{ababa}]$ of lengths $\{3, 5\}$).
   - Thus the $8$ nonempty palindromic substrings of $F_6$ are $\{\texttt{a}, \texttt{b}, \texttt{aba}, \texttt{aa}, \texttt{baab}, \texttt{abaaba}, \texttt{bab}, \texttt{ababa}\}$, one born at each index $r = 1, \dots, 8$.

3. **Autocorrelation Polynomial $C_{S,S}(x)$ & Expected Waiting Time $\mathbb{E}[T_S]$ ([`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)–[`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd))**:
   - The self-overlaps of $S = \texttt{abaababa}$ are $\operatorname{Overlap}(S, S) = \operatorname{Border}(S) \cup \{8\} = \{1, 3, 8\}$ (corresponding to periods $8 - k \in \{0, 5, 7\}$).
   - Hence the Guibas–Odlyzko autocorrelation polynomial and fair binary coin ($\sigma = 2$) waiting time are
     $$C_{S,S}(x) = \sum_{k \in \{1, 3, 8\}} x^{8-k} = 1 + x^5 + x^7, \qquad \mathbb{E}[T_S] = \sum_{k \in \{1, 3, 8\}} 2^k = 2^1 + 2^3 + 2^8 = 2 + 8 + 256 = 266.$$
